title: Workflow, Testing & CI
summary: How teams run Terraform for real: environment layouts (directories vs workspaces), DRY with modules and Terragrunt, linting and misconfiguration scanning, `terraform test` with mocks, pre-commit hooks, GitHub Actions with plan comments and OIDC to AWS, policy as code, drift detection, and provider/Terraform upgrades.
objectives: Choose between per-environment directories and workspaces, and explain the trade-offs
Keep configurations DRY with modules and know what Terragrunt adds
Run `terraform fmt`, `validate`, TFLint, Trivy and Checkov, locally and as pre-commit hooks
Write `.tftest.hcl` files with run blocks, assertions, `expect_failures` and `mock_provider`
Build a GitHub Actions pipeline that plans on pull requests, comments the plan, and applies on merge using OIDC instead of static AWS keys
Explain policy as code with OPA/Conftest and Sentinel, and write a simple Rego rule against a plan
Detect drift with `plan -detailed-exitcode` and `-refresh-only`, and decide how to resolve it
Apply team practices: plan review, small blast radius, state per component, pinned and regularly upgraded versions
